gen-gf-gugi-gf-miriam-libre: Tall, bold and cut open. Gugi's lowercase nearly climbs to its capitals, built to be noticed, while Miriam Libre, a sans-serif, keeps thin wire-like strokes and a sturdy lowercase.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Bold letters, cut wide open. Gugi earns its keep big and brief, where its tall lowercase shows off, while Mochiy Pop P One leaves wide gaps between its letters.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Noto Sans Tai Le reads gently, strokes tapering off before they touch. Across paragraphs it stays quiet and approachable, leaving Gugi to supply the bold, tall-lowercase swagger up top.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Loud, tall letters with open cuts. Noto Sans Ugaritic is the quiet one, its letter mouths left open like unjoined chalk arcs, while Gugi handles the loud stuff with curves meeting its stems.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-noto-san: Noto Sans Mono spaces its letters generously so none bump, with every curve opening wide, a sans-serif that feels contemporary. Love Ya Like A Sister earns its keep big and brief.
Bold neon glass, reshaped into letters. Love Ya Like A Sister makes the splash with that tubular stroke, while Noto Sans Old Italic keeps its curve endings well apart.
Noto Sans Tai Viet has short ascenders and a tall x-height, its terminals pulled back before each curve closes. Love Ya Like A Sister earns its place large and brief.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-batak: Wide-tracked, open-ended and loud. Offside makes its stand with untapered, widely spaced letters, while Noto Sans Batak, a sans-serif, brings a towering x-height and a wide e that never squeezes shut.
